questions.question: When reversing a singly linked list iteratively, why must you save `cur.next` before setting `cur.next = prev`?
options: Because otherwise the reference to the rest of the list is lost
To make the algorithm O(log n)
questions.explanation: Once cur.next is overwritten, nothing points to the remaining nodes. Saving it first lets you continue the walk.

questions.question: What problem does a dummy (sentinel) node before the head solve?
options: It makes access by index O(1)
It removes the need to special-case operations that change the head
questions.explanation: With a dummy, every real node has a predecessor, so insert/remove code works the same at the head as anywhere else. The real head is dummy.next.

questions.question: Which operation is O(1) for a singly linked list with head and tail pointers but O(n) for an array?
questions.explanation: Prepending just creates a node pointing at the old head. An array must shift every element. Removing the tail of a singly linked list is O(n) because you must find its predecessor.

questions.question: What is the space complexity of the recursive linked list reversal?
questions.explanation: It recurses once per node before unwinding, so n frames sit on the stack. The iterative version uses O(1) space.
